issue.title: Expire healthy inspector consent when the accepted API-key generation changes
issue.body:
Found as F1 in the independent GPT-6.2 Astra/xhigh source review of #416/#420 at local candidate `3c35b3d0f345dd420c67b90d59de94a2f73d946b`, compared with `0f6c325becf3e3e0562ae69dfae2c42bcf1d7129`.

The proposed inspector outage gates preserve the ordinary healthy path. In that path, an already-open review or a choice waiting before HTTP dispatch can survive an accepted API-key generation change on the same run. The API key is selected at dispatch, so a choice made under credential A may execute under credential B. The reviewer traced the path in `apps/web/src/runs/RunInspectorPage.tsx:307–313` and `apps/web/src/api/api-key.ts:66–75`; the healthy consent behavior also exists at the comparison base.

This is a source-supported scenario, **not an independently executed cross-credential reproduction or a demonstrated server authorization bypass**. Server authorization remains separate.

Expected outcome:

- Reproduce a healthy same-run accepted-key change with no preceding browser/API outage, including a change received from a second tab.
- An existing review must require fresh consent; a choice held before dispatch must send no request under the replacement credential.
- A new deliberate choice under the current credential can send once.
- Cover same-key reacceptance/new generation and preserve the healthy event-qualified header over a pending read.
- Record the actual authenticated actor through a controlled API fixture where needed; do not change server authorization or introduce a new actor kind.

Parked because #416 explicitly preserves ordinary healthy/loading behavior and addresses outage-scoped consent. This issue does not waive its introduced outage/recovery defects or any review, QA, coverage, CI or merge gate.

A bounded all-state duplicate search used credential+consent, API-key+review, actor+replay, credential+replay and generation+consent. #386 concerns header evidence; #415 concerns the never-produced MCP actor kind. Neither records this healthy consent-generation problem. No implementation or new delivery gate is admitted by this ticket.
